summary: Iter52 = MACRO REGRESSION AUDIT of SB Drive VTC (4 apps + admin + 9 service categories). Method: (1) grep of 40+ admin/driver/client pages to identify which ones actually call a backend API vs which ones render hardcoded mock data; (2) pytest reachability probe of 74 backend routes; (3) Playwright sweep of 49 admin URLs post-login to detect dead/placeholder screens. RESULT: admin dashboard + 18 wired pages work with real data (users=76, drivers=14, rides=87, recent rides stream live). BUT ~20+ admin pages are UNWIRED (hardcoded mock rows, no fetch at all), 6 'Settings & Utilities' routes fall through to a wrong default config, and ~10 driver-app endpoints that DriverHome / DriverEarnings / DriverDocuments rely on return 404. Top-20 blockers prioritized P0/P1/P2 below.

critical_code_review_comments: AdminServiceConfig.js line 107 — silent fallback to 'genie' means 13+ sidebar items ship identical Genie-labeled form; strictly never use a silent default for a multi-route dispatcher — throw or show a placeholder.
18 of the ~38 admin pages contain 0 fetch/axios/adminAPI calls — that's a 47% placeholder rate; any 'admin dashboard' claim is heavily aspirational.

Driver-app pages reference endpoints that don't exist; contract between frontend and drivers.py router was never finalized. Suggest adding a contract test that diff's UI fetch URLs vs registered FastAPI routes and fails CI if any URL 404s.

AdminCrudPages.js uses 'defaults' arrays baked into the source: first render shows defaults before fetch; if fetch fails, defaults stay — gives false impression of persistence. Replace with explicit empty-state.

Route aliasing in App.js (/admin/trips -> AdminRides, /admin/reviews -> AdminSupport, /admin/later-bookings -> AdminManualBooking, /admin/store-orders -> AdminOrders, /admin/store-delivery -> AdminOrders) — OK short-term but every alias is a navigation surprise.
AdminReferralSettings reads from /api/referral/stats (a USER-scoped endpoint) while sitting under admin — will show the admin's own referral data, not platform-wide.

context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration is a macro audit, not feature testing. Top-20 blockers are enumerated above, grouped P0/P1/P2. Key files with 0 API calls (hardcoded): AdminPromocodes, AdminBanners, AdminPayout, AdminSettlements, AdminDisputes, AdminWalletRequests, AdminDocuments, AdminGeoFence, AdminGodsView, AdminHeatView, AdminNewsletter, AdminTemplates, AdminSettings. Key admin routes that fall through to Genie config: /admin/payment-options, /admin/currency, /admin/language, /admin/seo, /admin/maps-api, /admin/country, /admin/state, /admin/pages, /admin/app-home, /admin/intro, /admin/labels, /admin/cancel-reasons, /admin/location-fare. Driver endpoints that 404: /api/drivers/my-stats, /my-earnings, /my-documents, /my-notifications, /incoming-requests. Recommend main agent address P0 items in batches (driver endpoints, then admin CRUD, then service-config fallthrough) before requesting another full sweep.
rca of the issue: This is a legacy-template situation: the React admin skeleton (sidebar labeled XJEKPLUS) was imported wholesale with many pages hardcoded for demo, and only ~47% of admin pages and ~60% of client endpoints were actually wired to the FastAPI backend. The team shipped the working surface (dashboard, users, drivers, rides, orders, stores, rewards, priority drivers) but left the remaining sidebar items as hardcoded placeholders or generic fall-through config. Driver-app pages reference endpoint names that were planned but never implemented — frontend and backend contracts diverged. Fix strategy: (a) for every admin page with 0 API calls, either delete the menu item or wire it to /api/admin/crud/{collection}; (b) add the 5 missing driver endpoints or re-point the UI to existing /api/drivers/earnings + /api/drivers/my-activity; (c) replace the silent Genie fallback in AdminServiceConfig with a typed placeholder; (d) seed realistic data so emptiness isn't confused with breakage.
